stories.title: Gartner (May 2026): 40% of Enterprises Will Decommission Production AI Agents by 2027 Due to Governance Gaps
stories.body: On May 26, 2026, Gartner published a forecast that by 2027, 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous AI agents — not because the technology failed, but because governance gaps are discovered only after a production incident occurs. Gartner's diagnosis is specific: applying a single, uniform governance standard across every agent regardless of its autonomy level and access scope is itself a primary cause of failure. This follows Gartner's separate projection that 40% of enterprise applications will embed task-specific AI agents by end of 2026, up from under 5% in 2025, meaning a large wave of under-governed agents is already entering production.
stories.why: This is the most powerful objection-handling stat in the market right now: pilots are graduating to production, then getting killed by governance failures, not AI capability gaps — exactly the 'pilot purgatory' problem Graas solves. Use it to shift the conversation from 'does the AI work?' to 'do you have the context layer, policy enforcement, and observability to keep it in production?'

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Have Stopped Buying Software to Build It With AI Coding Agents — but EBIT Impact Stays Flat at 37%
stories.body: McKinsey's State of AI 2026 survey of 1,719 organizations across 97 countries, published August 25, 2026, found that 32% of respondents decided against buying at least one software product or feature because agentic coding tools let them build it in-house instead — a figure that rises to nearly 50% among AI high performers. Despite this build momentum, the share of organizations attributing any EBIT impact to AI remained flat at 37%, unchanged from 2025, and only 6% qualify as high performers attributing 5%+ of EBIT to AI. Roughly one in five organizations also reported that AI operating costs are already constraining the scale of their AI use.
stories.why: The 'we'll build it ourselves' objection now has an analyst-grade counter: building is easy, but profit impact has stalled for two years because enterprises lack the data foundation to make agents reliable at scale. Graas can position its context and semantic layer as the missing ingredient between individual productivity gains (80% report these) and actual EBIT return.

stories.title: Gartner (September 2026): 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge' — Names Context Graph as the Foundational Layer for Agentic AI
stories.body: In a September 15, 2026 research note, Gartner identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in the declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge required to reason about enterprise tasks and decisions, with policies enforced through runtime constraints. Gartner distinguishes context graphs from simple graph databases, arguing that an enterprise-scale context graph must span operational data across all systems rather than serve a single use case. The note frames building a domain-specific, continuously updated context graph — encoding what the organization knows, how it works, and what it permits — as the prerequisite for moving agentic AI from experiment to enterprise scale.
stories.why: Gartner has now named and defined exactly what Graas sells. A seller can walk into any retail or CPG account and cite this Gartner research to validate that the context layer is not an optional add-on — it is what determines whether agents work or get decommissioned. It reframes Graas's architecture as analyst-endorsed infrastructure, not a niche vendor claim.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $950M at $15.8B Valuation, Launches 'Horizon' for Long-Running Agents, and Now Claims 40%+ of Fortune 50 Customers
stories.body: In May 2026, Sierra raised $950 million led by Tiger Global and GV at a valuation described as over $15 billion, bringing total funding to approximately $1.6 billion; the company reported over $150 million in ARR as of February 2026. In July 2026, Sierra launched 'Horizon' via its acquisition of Takeoff, extending agent capability to goals that unfold over days or weeks, and in August launched Voice Personas. Sierra now claims to serve more than 40% of the Fortune 50, with named enterprise customers including CarMax, ADT, WeightWatchers, and SiriusXM — all charged on outcome-based pricing estimated at roughly $1.50 per resolved interaction.
stories.why: Sierra is the most-cited competitor in enterprise customer-service AI and is now entering long-horizon, multi-day agentic workflows that overlap with Graas's territory in ordering, service escalation, and supply chain coordination. Sellers need to know Sierra's pricing model, customer list, and capability roadmap to position Graas's context-layer differentiation — specifically that Sierra agents still depend on external knowledge infrastructure that Graas provides.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Boosts In-Stocks by 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60% in CPG–Retail Collaboration Deployments
stories.body: A BCG analysis published in its 'Breaking Friction Silos' report found that agentic AI deployed across CPG and retailer supply chain workflows can boost in-stock rates by 2–4% and planning productivity by over 60%. BCG describes a multi-agent architecture where one sub-agent monitors store- and DC-level inventory signals against sell-through velocity and proactively generates replenishment recommendations before the retailer's own cycle catches a pending stockout, while a separate evaluation sub-agent scores recommendation quality before action and an observability layer provides an auditable record of every agent decision. A separate Tredence case study cited an agentic deduction-management solution integrated across 30+ systems that recovered $6.5M from roughly $40M in addressable trade deduction spend for one enterprise CPG client.
stories.why: These are concrete outcome numbers — the kind that move enterprise buying committees. The BCG architecture (inventory-monitoring agent + evaluation sub-agent + observability layer) maps directly to what Graas builds: a governed context layer is what allows the evaluation sub-agent to score recommendations against 'historical accuracy, current data completeness, and known edge cases.' Use this to show that the outcome numbers require the data foundation, not just the agent.
